title: Passgate template and SLA mapping review
summary: Quick sign-off on the POC acceptance artifacts: pass/fail gates (we called them 'passgates'), mapping of those gates to SLA thresholds, and the expected reporting bundle (CSV + dashboard + executive one-pager). Agreed measurement windows, sample sizes, and responsibilities. Action: Redwood to deliver benchmark template and initial runbook; customer to provide evaluation prompt set and baseline metrics.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-26
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah (Redwood); Mark Rivera, Jenna Li, Omar Diaz, Ravi Patel (QuantumPay)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE on this account. Priya from SE will drive the benchmarks section today. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Jenna Li: Doing good, thanks. Running a bit late, but we have the key people here.
[00:26] Priya Shah: great, quick agenda: define the "passgates" we talked about in the doc, align on measurement windows and sample sizes, agree on the report deliverables and handoffs. We'll cover what Redwood will deliver and what we need from QuantumPay.
[00:42] Mark Rivera: sounds good. Our main concerns remain: p95 latency for short payments workflows — that's critical — and hallucination rate on the authorization assistant. We'll also need to see cost projections at realistic throughput.
[01:05] Alex Kim: yep, understood. For clarity, when you say "short payments workflows"—what's your typical prompt/response size and concurrency?
[01:22] Omar Diaz: most calls are ~80-200 tokens in, 50-180 tokens out. Peak concurrency around 250 qps during end-of-day batch, steady 50-70 qps.
[01:35] Ravi Patel: and tolerances: we need p95 under 300ms for the critical path, ideally under 200ms. Anything above that we degrade user experience.
[01:48] Priya Shah: okay, good real numbers. For the POC passgates we propose: latency p95 target (short path) 200ms soft, 300ms hard; correctness threshold measured via sample eval set — F1 or exact-match depending on task — target >92% on labeled set; hallucination rate <2% on a curated set; throughput sustain 200 qps for 30 minutes without degradation; token cost target less than $0.40 per 1k tokens (we'll provide model variants and quantization profiles).
[02:20] Mark Rivera: can you explain the soft vs hard threshold language?
[02:28] Priya Shah: yeah, soft means we expect occasional breaches during early runs but we want trendline below that; hard means it's a blocker for go decision. We'll show both in the report.
[02:38] Jenna Li: makes sense. For accuracy, do you mean we provide the evaluation harness or we run it?
[02:45] Priya Shah: we'll provide the harness and runner containers, plus our benchmark template CSV. You provide the labeled eval set and the prompts representing the production distribution. Redwood will run the baseline and one tuned run and share raw output + analysis.
[03:02] Omar Diaz: what about data residency? Some of these prompts touch PII — we might need on-prem or VPC.
[03:11] Alex Kim: noted. We included the Private deployment option in previous emails. For the benchmark runs, we can do a blinded run in your VPC, or you can supply sanitized examples. For the POC acceptance, traces and audit logs will be redacted per your policy.
[03:30] Mark Rivera: we do want KMS integration and SOC2 evidence as part of the artifacts.
[03:36] Priya Shah: we'll include SOC2 attestation and KMS integration notes in the security appendix. For the runbook we'll also document key rotation and who has access to the benchmark outputs.
[03:48] Ravi Patel: back to measurement: what's the sample size to determine hallucination rate reliably?
[03:55] Priya Shah: we recommend at least 1,000 labeled examples for hallucination metrics with stratified sampling across templates; for latency and throughput, we need at least 30 minutes of sustained load at target qps and multiple runs at different concurrency.
[04:14] Jenna Li: 1,000? that's a lot, we have like 300 labeled examples currently. Can we do smaller and still have confidence?
[04:24] Mark Rivera: maybe we can bootstrap with 300 labeled and then run a second pass after we label another 500.
[04:31] Alex Kim: that's reasonable; we'll mark the acceptance as conditional: initial pass with 300 labeled to unblock early evaluation, full acceptance requires the 1,000 sample run. We'll capture that in the passgate matrix.
[04:44] Priya Shah: exactly. In the passgate matrix we'll include conditional pass states. For reporting, Redwood will deliver: a CSV of raw predictions (prompt, response, latency, tokens), a JSON summary (we can also produce CSV-only if you prefer), latency histograms, percentiles, and a one-page executive summary PDF. We'll also push time-series to your Grafana if you want real-time dashboards.
[05:12] Omar Diaz: Grafana pull is preferred. We already run Prometheus. What's the integration effort?
[05:20] Priya Shah: we have an exporter and a short config script. For the POC we can stand up a sandbox integration; full production needs a dedicated agent. We'll include config snippets in the runbook.
[05:34] Speaker 6: (muffled) cost — can you show a comparison of optimized quantized run vs full fp?
[05:41] Alex Kim: yes, we'll run three model variants: base fp32-like, quantized int8, and a distilled small model. We'll show throughput/latency/cost per 1k tokens, and a quality delta table.
[05:55] Jenna Li: about the reporting cadence — we want weekly reports during the POC and a final acceptance packet. What goes into the final packet?
[06:04] Priya Shah: final acceptance packet includes: passgate matrix with measurements and verdicts, raw CSV of runs, latency percentile graphs, cost calculations, a short technical appendix with config, and a remediation checklist if any gate fails.
[06:20] Mark Rivera: what's the definition of 'pass' at the end — do all gates need to be green?
[06:26] Alex Kim: typical setup: core gates (latency hard threshold, security controls, and hallucination hard threshold) must pass. Others can be on a conditional or soft pass with remediation plans. We'll label each gate as Pass / Conditional Pass / Fail with required actions.
[06:40] Ravi Patel: can you give an example of a conditional pass?
[06:44] Priya Shah: e.g., latency p95 at 220ms would become a conditional pass if other metrics are strong and we agree a configuration tweak (batching change or different kernel) reduces it to target within two weeks.
[06:54] Omar Diaz: who signs off? Jenna as CTO or Mark as Head of ML?
[06:58] Jenna Li: I can sign tech acceptance; procurement will need to sign commercial. For the POC go decision, we'll do a joint sign-off: ML + Platform + Product.
[07:10] Alex Kim: perfect. We'll capture signers in the acceptance doc.
[07:14] Priya Shah: timeline — Redwood will produce the benchmark template and runbook by next Friday, October 3. QuantumPay to provide a sanitized eval set and baseline metrics by October 8. We aim to complete runs and a draft report by Oct 15, review on Oct 16. Final acceptance by Oct 22. Does that align?
[07:36] Mark Rivera: aggressive but possible. Our labeling team can prioritize a 500-example expansion for the first run.
[07:44] Jenna Li: only caveat is legal needs to check the data transfer if Redwood is using hosted infra. Might push some runs into VPC.
[07:54] Alex Kim: understood, we'll plan both hosted and VPC variants and note any differences in the report.
[08:01] Speaker 6: transcription glitch - sorry.
[08:04] Priya Shah: Security checklist: we need confirmation of required certifications (SOC2 Type II), KMS for keys, SSO for users, and audit logs retention at least 90 days for POC.
[08:18] Jenna Li: SOC2 we require, and KMS yes. Audit logs we can accept 90 days for the POC.
[08:27] Omar Diaz: also need RBAC controls so only specific team members can pull raw predictions.
[08:32] Priya Shah: we'll include RBAC details and a sample role mapping in the runbook.
[08:38] Alex Kim: Competition question — who else are you evaluating?
[08:42] Mark Rivera: looking at Anthropic for safety, Vertex AI for speed at scale, and a small on-prem vendor for compliance.
[08:51] Alex Kim: ok, we can highlight differentiation in the handoff doc.
[08:55] Priya Shah: measurement specifics we'll include in the template: sample id, prompt template, ground truth, response, token counts (in/out), latency_ms, model_variant, quantization_flag, run_id. That CSV structure will let you slice by template and compute hallucination rates programmatically.
[09:15] Ravi Patel: for the cost model, can you include an estimated blended cost per 1M tokens for our projected monthly volume?
[09:23] Alex Kim: yes, include blended cost assuming X hours of peak and Y steady-state; we'll parameterize it so you can plug in your numbers.
[09:31] Jenna Li: reporting format: CSV + PDF + dashboard. Also ask that raw predictions be redacted for any PII fields before sharing externally.
[09:44] Priya Shah: we'll add a redaction step in the runbook and auto-mask fields matching regex rules; we'll also include a QA checklist for data handling.
[09:53] Mark Rivera: ok good. Let's capture action items now.
[09:58] Alex Kim: I'll read them out.
[10:00] Priya Shah: (typing)
[10:02] Alex Kim: Action 1: Redwood (Alex) to share benchmark CSV template, runbook, and a checklist by 2025-10-03.
[10:12] Alex Kim: Action 2: QuantumPay (Mark/Ravi) to share current labeled eval set and baseline metrics by 2025-10-08.
[10:19] Alex Kim: Action 3: Redwood (Priya) to run baseline + quantized run and produce draft report by 2025-10-15.
[10:27] Alex Kim: Action 4: Joint review meeting on 2025-10-16 to go over draft and decide remediation steps.
[10:34] Alex Kim: Action 5: QuantumPay to confirm security controls (KMS, RBAC mapping) and whether POC runs in VPC by 2025-10-06.
[10:44] Jenna Li: I will coordinate legal and get back by Oct 6.
[10:47] Mark Rivera: small question — will you share the raw latency histograms and the threshold code so we can reproduce the percentiles?
[10:55] Priya Shah: yes, we'll share the scripts and the exact percentile computation. We'll open a shared repo for reproducing the runs.
[11:04] Ravi Patel: what if the hallucination metric is 3% on the initial run? Is that auto fail?
[11:10] Priya Shah: if hallucination >2% on the 300-sample initial run, it's a conditional fail; we'll recommend model variant or prompt engineering adjustments and re-run. The final acceptance uses the 1,000-sample run to decide hard fail vs pass.
[11:24] Alex Kim: okay, signoff process again: ML lead, Platform, and Product will confirm. We'll prepare a one-page acceptance form for signatures.
[11:35] Jenna Li: good. Anything else?
[11:38] Mark Rivera: just confirm the test harness language — container images or scripts?
[11:43] Priya Shah: both: Dockerized runner + an optional k8s job manifest. We'll include a minimal local runner for smaller teams.
[11:52] Alex Kim: cool. We'll email the artifacts after this call. Thanks everyone.
[11:56] Jenna Li: thanks.
[11:57] Meeting end.
next_steps: Alex Kim - Send benchmark CSV template, runbook, and dashboard config by 2025-10-03
Mark Rivera / Ravi Patel - Provide sanitized labeled eval set and baseline metrics by 2025-10-08
Priya Shah - Execute baseline and quantized runs; deliver draft report by 2025-10-15
All - Join joint review on 2025-10-16 to review draft and decide remediation
Jenna Li - Confirm legal/data transfer constraints and VPC decision by 2025-10-06

Mark Rivera: Send current labeled sample of 300 examples and inventory (due 2025-10-08)
Ravi Patel: Coordinate product acceptance criteria signers (due 2025-10-10)
Priya Shah: Run baseline + quantized experiments and upload raw CSV (due 2025-10-15)
